model.name: Sex-specific log-density binomial logistic regression
model.likelihood: mosquitoes_infected_i ~ Binomial(mosquitoes_examined_i, p_i), independently by feed

diagnostics.model_comparison: Sex-specific AIC 778.498 versus total-gametocyte AIC 790.259 (Delta AIC total-minus-sex 11.760); sex-specific retained.
diagnostics.asexual_assessment: Adding log10(asexual density) to the sex-specific model: LR chi-square(1)=0.564, p=0.453, Delta AIC(add-minus-base)=1.436; no useful improvement, and no causal interpretation.
diagnostics.calibration: Feed-level binomial deviance 15.549 on 24 df (p=0.904); Pearson chi-square/df 0.600. No detected lack of fit, though only 27 feeds limit power.

literature.claim: Sex-specific female and male gametocyte densities jointly predicted mosquito infection in membrane feeds; low male density could constrain infection.
literature.citation: Bradley et al., Predicting the likelihood and intensity of mosquito infection from sex-specific Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte density, eLife (2018)

literature.claim: Pfs25 RT-qPCR was developed and validated for quantifying female P. falciparum gametocytes.
literature.citation: Schneider et al., Quantification of female and male Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes by reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR, Molecular and Biochemical Parasitology (2015)

literature.claim: Sex-specific qRT-PCR assays used Pfs25 for female and PfMGET for male gametocytes in human blood.
literature.citation: Wang et al., Assays for quantification of male and female gametocytes in human blood by qRT-PCR in the absence of pure sex-specific gametocyte standards, Malaria Journal (2020)

literature.claim: SBP1 qRT-PCR was a sensitive marker for asexual ring-stage parasites, with some mature-gametocyte expression noted.
literature.citation: Tadesse et al., Molecular Markers for Sensitive Detection of Plasmodium falciparum Asexual Stage Parasites and their Application in a Malaria Clinical Trial, American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (2017)
